events.title: XML-RPC protocol specified
events.summary: Dave Winer published the XML-RPC specification on July 19, 1998 — remote procedure calls over HTTP with XML-encoded payloads.
events.about: XML-RPC let programs on different machines call functions across the network — POST an XML body, get an XML response. Lighter than CORBA, simpler than rolling your own binary protocol. It powered early blogging tools, Frontier-to-Frontier scripting, and the path toward SOAP enterprise web services.

narrative.whyChosen: XML-RPC was the first widely deployed HTTP+XML RPC style that everyday developers could implement.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved the web could carry structured remote calls, not just hypertext pages.
narrative.problemSolved: Cross-platform apps needed a simple RPC layer when platform-specific event systems (Apple Events, DCOM) would not interoperate.
